title: Rapid Go‑Live Scenario Cookbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, scenario-driven playbook for short-cycle launches where product velocity requires a focused set of KPI smoke-tests, lightweight rollout gates, and clear contingency moves. Target audience: Product Ops, Release Engineers, Solutions Eng, and on-call SREs. Use when we need to go from staging->canary->ramped traffic in under 72 hours.

How to use this doc (quick):
1) Pick a scenario below that matches your risk profile (low/med/high).
2) Populate the small runway tracker (section: Runway + Owners).
3) Confirm owners for each gate and run the preflight checklist 2 hours before traffic shift.
4) Keep a running log in Slack #launch-ops with the tag [rapid-go-live].

Scenarios (pick one):
- Low risk: UX-only surface changes, existing model version, no infra changes. Gate = automated smoke tests + p95 latency.
- Medium risk: Model upgrade (minor), minor infra config (batch/window), Canary 5% -> 25% over 24h. Gate = quality eval on golden prompts + cost delta < 15%.
- High risk: New model family or quantization profile change, infra change (new node type), staged rollouts across regions. Gate = manual QA pass + canary metrics stable for 48h.

KPI smoke-tests (controller KPIs we watch during rollout):
- Availability: 99.9% during rollout window (critical). Alert at 99.7%.
- Error rate (API-level 5xx): baseline + 0.2% absolute or 2x baseline -> immediate rollback.
- p50/p95/p99 latency (ms): p50 within ±15% of baseline, p95 < 350ms common target (depends on region/model).
- Cost per 1k tokens: expected delta <= +20% for medium risk; if > +30% for more than 2 hours, investigate.
- Output quality: BLEU/ROUGE-style score or custom eval on 50 golden prompts. If quality drops > 3% absolute vs baseline -> freeze.
- Functional regressions: automated E2E smoke (login->generate->save) must pass 100%.
- Business signal: user-facing conversion or CTA click-through (if applicable) should not drop by >10%.

Runway + Owners (template to paste into sprint note):
- Launch name: <short name>
- Start (staging verification): YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- Canary start: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- Ramp schedule: e.g., 0% -> 5% (2h) -> 25% (24h) -> 50% (48h) -> 100% (72h)
- Primary owner: <name> (product)
- Infra owner: <name> (platform/serving-runtime)
- SRE on-call: <name> (pager)
- QA owner: <name>
- Escalation owner (exec): <name>

Preflight checklist (do this before canary):
- [ ] Staging smoke tests green (list URLs + test ids in slack).
- [ ] Canary routing policy configured (policy id / config reviewed).
- [ ] Monitoring dashboard created with listed KPIs and saved as a pulldown.
- [ ] Alerts set: latency, error-rate, cost-delta, quality-drop.
- [ ] Rollback runbook validated (config and steps present in runbook doc).
- [ ] Permission & quota check for Dedicated pools (if applicable).
- [ ] Stakeholder notification scheduled (CS, Sales if customer-visible).
- [ ] Postmortem owner assigned (always).

Gating rules (explicit):
- Gate 0 (smoke at 5%): 2h stable, error rate <= threshold, quality eval sample passes.
- Gate 1 (ramp to 25%): after 24h with p95 within target and cost delta acceptable.
- Gate 2 (50%): no systemic errors reported, business metrics stable for 48h.
- Emergency rollback: any SRE with pager or product owner can trigger immediate rollback.

Contingency plays (fast moves):
- Quick rollback: change routing policy to compatible previous model variant (docs: runbook/rollback). Time to live: target < 3 minutes for routing change.
- Scoped fallback: divert only high-latency regions to previous model while keeping others live.
- Token-throttle: apply rate limit to non-critical routes to reduce load while investigating.
- Cost cap-trigger: if cost delta sustained, autoscale down dedicated pool or shift traffic to cheaper region (manual unless preconfigured).

Monitoring & dashboards (minimum queries):
- api.errors.rate_by_model (1m) + alert if spike.
- api.latency.p95_by_route (5m) + trendline.
- billing.token_cost_hourly (1h) + drift alert.
- eval.quality.golden_prompts (manual job run) -> attach summary to slack.

Quick smoke eval recipe (50 golden prompts):
1) Pull last stable golden set from /confluence link (see linked_artifacts).
2) Run eval job (instructions in Runbook).
3) Aggregate automated metrics (similarity/QA pass) and attach first 10 failures to Slack thread.
4) Manual spot-check 5 failures within 30 min for triage.

Decision table (simplified):
- If error rate > threshold and any user-facing outage -> rollback.
- If quality drop > 5% and persists for > 1h -> pause ramp and investigate.
- If cost delta > 30% and trending -> throttle non-critical traffic and notify finance.

Notes to reviewers / unknowns (explicit callouts):
- We do not currently have automated region-based fallback in the routing service; manual steps required.
- Canary traffic weight targets assume we have stable autoscaling; validate with Infra.
- Do we want a soft signal for hallucination increase? We need a lightweight hallucination proxy metric for some LLM outputs; filing RDW-927 as follow up.

Post-launch (24h & 7d checklist):
- 24h: confirm all dashboards show stable metrics, create a short launch summary and attach to the Jira ticket.
- 72h: run full golden prompt eval (1000 prompts) and compare to prelaunch baseline; triage any drift.
- 7d: business KPI readout and suggested follow-up improvements (Optimize suggestions: batching/quantization adjustments if cost too high).

Lightweight templates to copy:
- Slack status update (use template): [rapid-go-live] Canary started: <name> | 5% -> owner: <name> | dashboard: <url>
- Rollback one-liner: Rollback initiated by <name>. Routing reverted to <model-id>. Incident ticket: <jira-id>.

Appendix A — Example thresholds (example numbers, adapt per product):
- Baseline availability: 99.95% -> Rollback if <99.7%
- Error-rate baseline: 0.08% -> Alert if >0.5%
- p95 latency baseline: 220ms -> Alert if >350ms
- Cost per 1k tokens baseline: $1.10 -> Investigate if >$1.50 sustained

Appendix B — Short runbook links and owners: (copy into your launch note)
- Rollback runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/rollback-runbook
- Routing policy doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/routing-policies
- Monitoring dashboard proto: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/quick-launch-proto

End notes: Keep this doc short and pragmatic. If you're planning a multi-week or multi-region rollout, use the full Launch Playbook (linked in linked_artifacts) instead. Feedback welcome — ping me (Priya) or drop suggestions directly in the Confluence draft.
